newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end lower on money policy concerns.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end lower on money policy concerns.

text.p: Taiwan share prices closed lower on Monday, hit by a report of a possible tightening of money policy by the central bank, although the bank distanced itself from key elements of the report, brokers said.
The weighted index ended 55.32 points or 0.77 percent lower at 7,156.96. Turnover was only T$48.9 billion, far below the T$100 billion-plus levels reached in many January sessions.

Prices were hit by an Economic Daily News report on Monday quoting central bank vice governor Hsu Chia-tung as saying the bank would have to tighten monetary policy if the cabinet backs a 3.0 percent 1997 inflation target, below its own 3.3 target.
Hsu clarified his comments in an interview with Reuters.

"If the Council for Economic Planning and Development insists (on accepting a 3.0 percent CPI target) and the cabinet supports it, only then will the central bank hold a meeting to reconsider the target," Hsu told Reuters by telephone.
"We want to maintain a stable-to-loose monetary policy, hoping to help the economic situation," Hsu said.
Brokers said the cabinet-level row over CPI targets would make investors cautious, but tis impact should be short-lived.
"The dispute on CPI targets should be only a short-term factor," said HSBC Wardley James Capel analyst Alex Chen.
"After all, the economic recovery is slower than expected and the market expects the central bank to lower banks' reserve requirements after the Chinese new year (on February 7)."
The central bank has pledged to would lower banks' reserve requirements in "appropriate time" in 1997.
Paper shares fell most, followed by car and textile stocks.

The share index fell despite disclosure on Monday of the finding of government pollsters and economists that the economy was in a "green light" condition in December for the second straight month, indicating a possible recovery.
